text:
That confirms it — forcing required tool choice means the model can never reply with plain text after a decline, so it keeps calling tools until maxTurns errors out. The fix is to switch toolChoice from 'required' to 'auto' (or drop it entirely) so the model can respond conversationally once appropriate.

I should also consider adding a short system prompt instruction for the decline case — telling the model to reply briefly instead of re-calling approveRefund — since auto mode alone might not guarantee it stops looping back to the tool. But the core bug and snippet to fix is the toolChoice line itself.

I'll change toolChoice from 'required' to 'auto', matching the triage agent's explicit style. I'm weighing whether to also add system prompt guidance for post-decline behavior, but decide to keep the fix minimal since 'auto' already gives the model freedom to reply after a decline rather than re-calling tools.

I should note in my summary that I left the prompt unchanged and couldn't test end-to-end without an API key — let me check if one's available in the environment.
Confirmed: `'required'` maps to Gemini's `FunctionCallingMode.ANY`, so the model must call a tool on every turn. I'll check whether a Gemini API key is available so I can test the flow end to end.

text:
The root cause is `toolChoice: 'required'` on `refundAgent` in `src/agents.ts`. I changed it to `'auto'`, and `answer.json` is written in the project root.

`'required'` makes Gemini force a tool call on every turn. After the supervisor declined, the desk could only call tools again, so it re-asked for approval until `maxTurns` ran out and never produced a reply. I reproduced this before the change: the agent re-raised `approveRefund` on every step with empty output. After the change, a declined request ends with "Your refund for order A-1001 was not approved because there is a duplicate claim." with no further interrupts.

I did not change the system prompt, so it still has no explicit instruction for what to say after a decline. The model's reply came out short in my one test, but I didn't run it many times. I removed the `.genkit/` folder my test runs created and didn't touch `package.json`.
